    Required labeled sample size for PPI++ (mean or regression/contrast inference)

    n_required_ppi_pp.Rd

    Computes the minimum labeled sample size \(n\) required to achieve a desired statistical power for Prediction-Powered Plus (PPI++) inference.

    This function supports:

    1. Mean estimation

    Estimating a scalar parameter \(\theta = \mathbb{E}[Y]\) using prediction-powered estimators with augmentation weight \(\lambda\).

    2. Regression contrast estimation

    Estimating a linear contrast \(a^\top \beta^\star\) in either:

    • OLS (ordinary least squares)

    • GLM with canonical link (e.g., logistic or Poisson regression)

    via sandwich/Fisher blocks computed on labeled and unlabeled samples.

    The augmentation weight \(\lambda\) may be:

    • "vanilla" — \(\lambda = 1\) (standard PPI)

    • "user" — user-specified \(\lambda\)

    • "oracle" — variance-minimizing \(\lambda^\star(n)\) that depends on \(r = n/N\)

    The unlabeled sample size \(N\) contributes predictions \(f(X)\) that lower the estimator variance.

    n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta,
  N,
  alpha = 0.05,
  power = 0.8,
  type = c("mean", "regression"),
  lambda_mode = c("vanilla", "oracle", "user"),
  lambda_user = NULL,
  sigma_y2 = NULL,
  sigma_f2 = NULL,
  cov_y_f = NULL,
  var_f = NULL,
  var_res = NULL,
  metrics = NULL,
  metric_type = NULL,
  m_labeled = NULL,
  correction = TRUE,
  c = NULL,
  H_L = NULL,
  H_U = NULL,
  Sigma_YY = NULL,
  Sigma_ff_l = NULL,
  Sigma_ff_u = NULL,
  Sigma_Yf = NULL,
  warn_smallN = TRUE,
  smallN_threshold = 500,
  mode = c("error", "cap")
)

    Arguments

    delta

    Numeric scalar. Effect size being tested.

    • Mean case: difference from the null, \(\theta - \theta_0\).

    • Regression case: \(a^\top \beta - \theta_0\). Must be nonzero.

    N

    Positive scalar. Number of unlabeled observations providing predictions.

    alpha

    Significance level (two-sided). Default: 0.05.

    power

    Desired statistical power. Default: 0.80.

    type

    "mean" or "regression". "regression" covers both OLS and canonical GLM contrasts.

    lambda_mode

    "vanilla", "oracle", or "user".

    lambda_user

    Scalar specifying \(\lambda\) when lambda_mode = "user".

    sigma_y2

    Variance of labeled outcomes \(\Var(Y)\).

    sigma_f2

    Variance of predictions \(\Var(f(X))\).

    cov_y_f

    Covariance \(\Cov(Y, f(X))\).

    var_f

    Optional alias for sigma_f2.

    var_res

    Residual variance \(\Var(Y - f(X))\).

    metrics

    List of predictive metrics such as:

    • mse

    • r2

    • var_y

    • p_y (binary)

    • bias Required when direct moments are not supplied.

    metric_type

    "continuous" or "binary". Determines how metrics is interpreted.

    m_labeled

    Number of labeled samples used to compute prediction metrics.

    correction

    Logical; apply finite-sample adjustment when deriving metrics.

    c

    Contrast vector \(a\).

    H_L

    Labeled Hessian/Fisher block.

    H_U

    Unlabeled Hessian/Fisher block.

    Sigma_YY

    Labeled covariance block \(\Sigma_{YY}\).

    Sigma_ff_l

    Labeled covariance block \(\Sigma_{ff}\).

    Sigma_ff_u

    Unlabeled covariance block \(\Sigma_{ff}\).

    Sigma_Yf

    Cross-covariance \(\Sigma_{Yf}\).

    warn_smallN

    Logical. Warn when N < smallN_threshold.

    smallN_threshold

    Numeric. Default 500.

    mode

    "error" or "cap". "cap" returns n = N with an "achieved_power" attribute.

    Value

    Integer required sample size n_star. If capped, returns N with attribute "achieved_power".

    Examples

    
## Example 1: Using prediction metrics
metrics <- list(
  type   = "continuous",
  mse    = 0.6,
  var_y  = 1.0,
  m_obs  = 300
)

n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta       = 0.25,
  N           = 5000,
  type        = "mean",
  metrics     = metrics,
  metric_type = "continuous",
  lambda_mode = "vanilla"
)
#> [1] 77


## Example 2: Direct-moment supply
n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta      = 0.25,
  N          = 5000,
  type       = "mean",
  sigma_y2   = 1.0,
  sigma_f2   = 0.4,
  cov_y_f    = 0.18,
  lambda_mode = "oracle"
)
#> [1] 116


## Generate synthetic blocks for a 3-D contrast
p <- 3
cvec <- c(1, 0, -1)
Hpop <- diag(p)
SYY  <- diag(p)
Sff  <- 0.5 * diag(p)
SYf  <- 0.3 * diag(p)

## Vanilla λ = 1
n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta       = 0.15,
  N           = 2000,
  type        = "regression",
  c           = cvec,
  H_L         = Hpop,
  H_U         = Hpop,
  Sigma_YY    = SYY,
  Sigma_ff_l  = Sff,
  Sigma_ff_u  = Sff,
  Sigma_Yf    = SYf,
  lambda_mode = "vanilla"
)
#> [1] 761

## Oracle λ*
n_required_ppi_pp(
  delta       = 0.15,
  N           = 2000,
  type        = "regression",
  c           = cvec,
  H_L         = Hpop,
  H_U         = Hpop,
  Sigma_YY    = SYY,
  Sigma_ff_l  = Sff,
  Sigma_ff_u  = Sff,
  Sigma_Yf    = SYf,
  lambda_mode = "oracle"
)
#> [1] 602
